subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord preflight adopt strict active-target scoping that suppresses the current/default agent when another configured agent, role target, quoted mention, or configured bot sender means the current agent is not being addressed?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but the fix changes stable Discord routing precedence, role semantics, and bot-loop suppression for existing multi-agent guild setups.

options.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
options.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and prove it with focused tests plus live multi-bot Discord evidence.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Keep this issue as coordination while separate issues own reply-target precedence, role-trigger behavior, slash-command targeting, and bot-authored implicit-reply slices.

options.title: Keep current default-owner behavior
options.body: Document current routing plus opt-in `ignoreOtherMentions` and `allowBots` behavior as the intended contract, then close conflicting narrower requests after maintainer confirmation.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and prove it with focused tests plus live multi-bot Discord evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the central inbound mention policy and have the strongest history signal on the affected Discord routing contract.
